searchText: I think what you want is a forum like Ethereum Magicians or Ethereum Research. IMO, chat shouldn't be expected to be persistent. When I'm championing an EIP, I always try to summarize discussion into a post on the discussions-to link of the EIP. That way people don't have to read a lengthy chat or have access to Discord. Similar to how if I had a discussion in-person or via voice call I would summarize the outcomes of that into a more permanent and searchable location. The trouble is that a lot more than chat happens here. Serious discussions happen here, and there is no other record. Gitter had its problems, but when people asked why decisions were made - including people on core devs calls - we could link back to the relevant discussions there. > and there is no other record I think this is the core of the problem. Anytime serious discussion happens here and decisions are made the discussion **_should_** be summarized and the conclusions described in a more permanent location. If people are having discussions here and *not* propagating that information to more permanent sources I think that is bad. The same is true for traditional businesses where in-person discussions **should** be summarized and recorded somewhere more permanent than a verbal conversation (which is incredibly transient). I don't think the solution in the traditional world is to record all voice conversations, it is to follow the practice of recording summaries. **EIP-1559 Implementers' call in ~24.5 hours (Thursday Jan 14 at 16:00 UTC)** Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/234 Zoom: To be share here before the call What tends to happen is that on allcoredev calls there is a small amount of discussion and decisions are made that ratify consensus already achieved in discussions on the allcoredevs channel. Without a way to refer back to these discussions it's not clear how consensus was achieved. And without a way for people to easily follow these discussions we get accused of blindsiding people with our decisions. <@!301186049323958275> I wrote this as a starting point. https://notes.ethereum.org/rAAKzsBBRYC3fr42QM1ZIw Having a "best practices" document and re-enforcing this as our "culture" may go a long way. Thanks <@364458974906548225>. Another existing practice for EIP discussion is the https://ethereum-magicians.org/ forum. These tend to be discussions of _what_ the content of an EIP is, whereas here we tend discuss _whether_ and _when_ to implement it? Yeah, I would like to get better documentation of the ACD calls as well that includes more than just a transcript. Like a summary of what consensus was and how it was determined on specific topics. With just a transcript, it can be difficult to find answers to questions like you were asking above. That's what the numbered Decisions and Action Items are for. In part. Have "we" tried paying someone to do this? Fat chance 😉 Pin it? Backing way up - is it just a Discord preferences or bot thing for links like https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/798942537883844638 to be easily accessible? What do you mean? You can generate a link like that by right clicking on any message and choosing "copy link" (or on mobile choosing share and then copy to clipboard). Assuming we have not tried having an official note taker and "summarizer" for the ACD call, I think this is something we should pursue. Before I go actually seeking candidates, curious to hear from other call organizers on this idea. Griffin has done this for us for the Stateless calls and it's been awesome. I'd advocate for this to be a paid position. Probably 3 hours of work per call. 1.5 hours to actually attend the call. Another 1.5 hours to summarize. Summaries should be more than just a summary of the conversation. They should include things like supporting links to EIPs, forum posts, other supporting material. Final deliverable should probably be a markdown document committed to the `ethereum/pm` repository. Do you mean making links like that work without logging in to Discord? If so I don't think that is possible. You would need a bot to mirror the channel externally (such bots exist). Yes, that is what I mean. <@642887713246150666> or <@!187490121698770945> may be the right people to talk to about this before proceeding much more. I personally dislike discord links. Unless you "discord" all your devices, you tend to land on a login form (I don't log into discord in my browsers) Exactly. On Gitter people could easily use Github or Twitter login. (Yuck to gitter too. conceptually/ideologically 👍 . practically the UX wasn't nearly as polished as I've been spoiled to expect) Maybe it's gotten better. Recent stuff using Matrix is also intriguing (both gitter and Matrix itself) Email worked. Usenet worked. IRC worked. Standard protocols, lots of servers and archives, clients with whatever UX you preferred. Now we have proprietary protocols and I'm forced to learn a new UX every few months and use five or six of them every day that don't connect to each other. 50 years and no real progress. But I'm a whiny old man ... So, practical request - a way to make our discussions here more transparent - easily linked to and readable by the large number of people who care about what we have to say. 👆 is something that could easily be outsourced (if you are looking to spend EF money on something <@364458974906548225>). Would just be a simple Discord bot that mirrors somewhere (S3, IPFS, whatever) and has a tiny little web-app and help bot that will convert Discord links to externally accessible links. Bigger project if you want to also include reactions and edits in the extracted file, but not too much bigger. Easier, if possible - read-only OAuth access to this Discord server. I don't believe that is possible. 😦 Walled gardens. We thought we had killed then with the AOL battle. It is unfortunate that walled gardens are profitable while open platforms is not. It leads to the high quality software being walled gardens. 😢 Witness Facebook and Twitter. Discord is feature rich (reactions, quotes, replies, code blocks, inline code, syntax highlighting, channels, moderation tools, message pinning, RBAC, etc.) because it has a large team of people developing for it, who are paid for by the product which is successful partly because it is a walled garden. Yeah. We could go on and on. It's the proprietary protocols that wall us in. Clients compete on features but lock you in. Whereas Web browsers are feature-rich but all use the same protocol, so there are lots to choose from on lots of devices. Anyway, I have code to write so I can scan our blockchain to gather stats to analyze for faster syncing opportunities... Is EIP-2565: ModExp Gas Cost going into berlin? As far as I am aware, there are a few places where ACD meeting notes/summary are captured. For Jan 8 meeting - - Tim's tweet: https://twitter.com/TimBeiko/status/1347540679765811200 - Notes: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/pull/238 - Reddit: https://www.reddit.com/r/ethfinance/comments/ktl91o/daily_general_discussion_january_9_2021/gio1hym/?context=3 ACD Notes which are submitted to the Ethereum GitHub are actually being paid (Thanks to Moloch Grant) Thanks <@!642887713246150666> . I should have looked myself. That would have been easy to find. last mention of 2565 i see is acd 101 and it *is* on the list of berlin EIPs https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/325a5f1c59ff202627481ccebac9ba63f3c2896f/All%20Core%20Devs%20Meetings/Meeting%20101.md#1d-final-go-no-go-for-berlin-eips No problem! Just for information, Ethereum Cat Herders are documenting notes for ACD, Eth2, EIPIP & 1559 meetings. So, if there is any concern, happy to answer 🙂 <@!543900561460822016> - yes it is scheduled for Berlin. I need to submit a PR to mark it Final There was a google sheets document that had it listed that I believe <@!642887713246150666> may have created I don't recommend final until it ships, in case last minute changes are required. It definitely should be in review though, and maybe even Last Call if you are pretty confident that no more changes will land before launch. Ah ok, thanks <@!301186049323958275> - I thought in an all core devs about a month or so ago it was recommended that it it be bumped. It is in last call currently
